selected.description: When a question asks what someone read, used, owned, or was engaged in during a time period, search across event, preference, and state memories without strict point-time filtering, because ongoing activities are often recorded as preferences or states.

nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks which holiday, holiday season, or time of year coincides with a specific event, retrieve the event and its date first, then infer the season from the date; do not stop after one search that misses the event.
content: When a question asks which holiday, holiday season, or time of year coincides with an event (e.g., wedding, birthday, trip), first retrieve the event memory and its world_start date. Use event synonyms (got married/wedding, was born/birthday) and do not require the holiday or season name to appear in the query or memory text.

If the event memory provides a date but no holiday name, determine the holiday or season from the calendar date (e.g., late December → Christmas season) using general world knowledge, and answer from that date as evidence.

Do not conclude 'No information available' after a single retrieval when the question asks about an event's temporal context; run at least one additional search focused on the event and its date before answering.
